item.title: From pilot to public good: Opening up the nature-based solutions opportunity scan
item.description: The Nature-Based Solutions Opportunity Scan, developed by the World Bank and the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR), uses globally available Earth observation data to identify nature-based solutions (NBS) investment opportunities.

item.title: Extreme weather risk is scaring big corporations away from poorer countries – that hurts the companies, too
item.description: As climate change increases the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events around the world, these effects can be especially severe in poorer countries that lack the resources to prepare for disasters or recover quickly after they hit.

item.title: El Niño threatens health, too – early warnings done right can save lives
item.description: When warnings pair information about the risk with practical actions and local resources, they can empower people rather than leaving them feeling helpless in the face of a disaster.

item.title: Protecting small businesses from extreme heat: a priority for COP31
item.description: This blog explores the escalating threat extreme heat poses to small businesses. It highlights economic vulnerabilities, evaluates current policy shortcomings leading into COP31.

item.title: Meet the 2026 WIN DRR Excellence Award Finalists
item.description: Meet the 10 WIN DRR Excellence Award finalists 2026 who stand for all the amazing women who are putting the Sendai Framework and its Gender Action Plan into practice across Asia and the Pacific.

item.title: Many regions have warmed beyond 1.5°C and some beyond 2°C, study finds
item.description: A study, published in Nature Climate Change, indicates that at the regional level, many places on Earth have already surpassed 1.5°C (2.7°F), and suggests that other regions have warmed as much as 2°C (3.6°F) due to human-caused climate change.

item.title: Resilience4Ports (R4P) indicators: Guidance notes
item.description: This guide explains the Resilience4Ports (R4P) Indicators, a framework for ports to assess climate and disaster resilience using 22 indicators and 10 quantitative metrics, identify priorities, and track progress.

item.title: Global trends in climate change litigation: 2026 snapshot
item.description: This report’s ninth annual snapshot examines global climate litigation and more than 3,600 cases in 62 countries. Courts increasingly recognize government climate obligations and corporate claims, but judgments need political will and legal follow-through

item.title: Policy frameworks for early warning systems (EWS)
item.description: This report examines how different countries have designed and implemented the policy frameworks that underpin their mobile-enabled early warning systems.

item.title: Madagascar’s early warning system: an assessment of SMS alert performance
item.description: This report examines the performance of SMS alerts within Madagascar’s national early warning system.

item.title: COP31 leaders back a long-term future for Early Warnings for All
item.description: At COP31, UN Secretary-General António Guterres and member states recognized the partnership behind the Early Warnings For All initiative's progress, and asked for the work to continue well past 2027.

item.title: Leading change for national resilience: Lessons from Canada
item.description: Shared responsibility for reducing disaster risk does not emerge from strategies alone. It depends on whether people understand the risk, commit to act, gain the skills to act and sustain new behaviours over time.

item.title: Assessing the climate justice case for catastrophe bonds
item.description: This issue brief explores the climate justice case for catastrophe bonds and how, with some design improvements, these financial instruments can become a tool to more equitably support post-disaster recovery and fund climate resilience.

item.title: Lecturer in risk perception and communication
item.description: The main purpose of the role is to carry out research, teaching and administration within the RDR, especially in areas related to risk perception and/or risk communication but also across the wider field of risk and disaster reduction.

item.title: Call for inputs for the first regular report on loss and damage
item.description: The Santiago Network Secretariat is launching a global call for inputs to support the development of the inaugural regular report on loss and damage associated with the adverse effects of climate change.

item.title: Building back better in small and remote Nordic-Arctic communities: a practitioner-oriented assessment checklist
item.description: This research brief brings key elements from Building Back Better (BBB) policies, guidelines and recovery-readiness approaches together in a compact, settlement-scale assessment toolbox.

item.title: University Centre of the Westfjords (UW)
item.description: The University Centre of the Westfjords, UW, is the smallest institution operating on an university level in Iceland and offers two international master's programmes which are accredited through the state-run University of Akureyri.

item.title: Ahead of COP31, UNHCR warns nearly 90 million displaced people face severe climate risks
item.description: According to UNHCR's latest report, nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people – three in four globally – are living in countries facing high to extreme exposure to climate-related hazards, including severe droughts, deadly floods and extreme heat.

item.title: IEA launches Global Observatory to help strengthen energy sector resilience
item.description: New data hub tracks energy system disruptions, maps risks to energy infrastructure and maintains a repository of measures and policies to help strengthen resilience worldwide

item.title: New IDF-UK “Insurance Partnership for Development” to drive use of disaster risk management, unlock investment and economic growth in emerging markets and developing economies
item.description: The objective of the Partnership is to enable Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDEs), especially low- and middle-income countries, to better prepare financially for shocks – strengthening resilience and unlocking investment and economic growth.

item.title: UNESCO and Eni México promote an educational proposal in Tabasco primary schools to strengthen resilience to climate change and disaster risk
item.description: Experiences from 13 primary schools in Sánchez Magallanes, supported by UNESCO and Eni México, offer proposals to strengthen climate adaptation in coastal areas.

item.title: World’s wettest rainstorms are getting wetter, affecting flood and drought risk
item.description: Events that deliver about half of global rainfall are getting shorter but more intense, with wide-ranging implications.

item.title: Understanding disaster risk: Disaster risk
item.description: Disaster risk is expressed as the likelihood of loss of life, injury or destruction and damage from a disaster in a given period of time.

item.title: Less rain, more intense storms: Climate change strengthens extreme urban floods
item.description: Preparing for a drier future does not mean preparing for milder floods. Cities need to prepare for contradictory challenge of managing both declining water availability and increasingly destructive rainfall extremes.

item.title: Regulation is key to a climate-resilient insurance market: How regulation can balance insurer interests and public resilience in the face of escalating climate risks
item.description: This report compares climate insurance regulation in seven jurisdictions, assessing prudential safeguards and consumer resilience. It finds none strong on both, with gaps in monitoring insurer withdrawals and aligning investment with resilience.

item.title: Strengthening global supply chains against El Niño and extreme weather events
item.description: An analysis of El Niño's impacts on global supply chains, highlighting supplier, logistics, and trade-route vulnerabilities while providing tools to assess risks and improve resilience.

item.title: Competency-based public health emergency and disaster management training for district teams in Uttarakhand, India: A mixed-methods evaluation of knowledge outcomes
item.description: This publication explores sub-national capacity for public health emergency and disaster management (PHEDM) in Uttarakhand, India.

item.title: Pro-Gender Support Foundation Pakistan
item.description: Their mission is to advance inclusive development by strengthening communities, building capacity, expanding opportunities and enabling meaningful participation for all, with a particular focus on transgender persons and other marginalized gender groups.

item.title: Understanding disaster risk: Vulnerability
item.description: Vulnerability is the human dimension of disasters and is the result of the range of economic, social, cultural, institutional, political and psychological factors that shape people’s lives and the environment that they live in.

item.title: Understanding disaster risk: Hazard
item.description: Understanding what hazards are, how they behave and interact, and how we can lessen their impact.

item.title: European tourism demand in the face of climate change: asymmetric impacts, demand reallocation, and deseasonalisation strategies
item.description: This study, using data from 1315 European regions and considering a tourism-specific climate index and tourism typologies, examines the potential impact of climate change on tourism demand across the continent under four warming scenarios.

item.title: Climate risks to health and nutrition in Togo: targeted analytics
item.description: This report assesses climate-related health and nutrition vulnerabilities in Togo, where rising temperatures, flooding, rainfall variability, drought, and sea-level rise are intensifying existing health challenges.

item.title: Disaster risk finance in Belize: Progress and perspectives
item.description: This report assesses Belize’s progress in strengthening disaster risk finance and provides recommendations for improving the country’s financial resilience to climate and disaster-related shocks.

item.title: Assessing the feasibility of linking social protection with anticipatory action: The case of Zimbabwe
item.description: This publication presents a regional project to strengthen early warning and anticipatory action (AA) systems, with Zimbabwe serving as a key case study.

item.title: Community involvement in wildfire risk reduction through a social contract lens: A case study in Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada
item.description: This paper applies social contract theory to wildfire risk-reduction in Yellowknife after the 2023 evacuation, finding unclear roles, mismatched resources and inconsistent inclusion hinder collaboration and long-term planning.

item.title: Advancing mobile early warnings at scale: A regional partnership model for the Pacific Islands
item.description: A unique partnership between the GSMA and the Pacific Islands Telecommunications Association (PITA) is advancing the implementation of mobile-enabled Early Warning Systems (EWS) through Cell Broadcast across the Pacific Islands.

item.title: How does building climate-resilient cities affect food production: Evidence from pilot policies in China
item.description: This study uses multi-period difference-in-differences analysis to find China’s Climate-Resilient Cities Policy increases per capita grain production beyond urban areas, with stronger effects along the Hu Huanyong Line and in resource-based cities.

item.title: Unlocking Universal Service Funds for early warning systems: Lessons from Thailand and Argentina
item.description: Thailand and Argentina demonstrate how Universal Service Funds can finance nationwide cell broadcast early warning systems, offering a scalable model to overcome funding barriers and expand life-saving disaster alerts globally.

item.title: Building disaster resilience through mobile-enabled early warning systems in Asia Pacific
item.description: Mobile technology, public-private partnerships, and innovative financing are strengthening disaster resilience and scaling inclusive, mobile-enabled early warning systems across Asia Pacific.

item.title: New version of Climate Pulse provides new monitoring of El Niño conditions
item.description: The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) has released Climate Pulse 2.0, adding dedicated monitoring of the main El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) regions and historical maps back to 1940 for air temperature.
